replies.name: #248 Restore moderated Webmentions and IndieWeb article metadata
replies.content:
<!-- BEGIN_TEDT_WEBMENTION_VERIFICATION -->
Live Webmention verification for tedt.org, UPDATED stage, October 25, 2026. This temporary source checks a [TedT.org article](https://tedt.org/Dungeons-and-Dragons-5th-Edition-Rules-For-Gamma-World-Weapons/) and [Webmention Rocks discovery test 1](https://webmention.rocks/test/1). Software: [TedT.org standalone IndieWeb sender](https://github.com/TedTschopp/tedt.org/blob/be08fb93d4d699e73341018738627ddc3c5596e7/_code/indieweb.rb). This verification block will be removed after testing.
<!-- END_TEDT_WEBMENTION_VERIFICATION -->

Article Webmention forms currently submit relative targets, and response display depends on a live browser-side provider request. This change submits each article's absolute canonical URL and renders approved responses during the Jekyll build.

- Recover 15 trusted public Webmentions across canonical and legacy aliases; hold unfamiliar sources for review (currently ID 1747977). Keep replies, mentions, likes, reposts, bookmarks, RSVPs, and follows separate. Discard provider HTML and private records, escape displayed text, and retain the cache if a complete refresh fails.
- Add accessible progressive submission feedback, usable native forms without JavaScript, explicit article/author/date metadata, homepage identity fixes, and a chronological `/updates/` h-feed that respects web publication dates.
- Refresh incoming responses hourly. Send outgoing notifications from the successful Pages artifact after checking the public source; retain edit/removal targets, retry transient failures, and baseline existing articles without notifying their historical links. Store receipts on `indieweb-state` so main's deployment checks continue to work. Keep downloaded artifacts in runner temporary storage and consume regular article entries as bounded data, with separate deployment and retry jobs.
- Reuse the merged Mastodon pipeline's verified `mastodon-post-url` values for `u-syndication`. Preserve its renderer and rollout controls. Cache-only deployments skip social cross-posting. Correct the publication-date test's assumption that every source-dated quote is pre-2003, including the newly added Sean Grove quote.

Validation:
- Hosted [Site Quality + Deploy](https://github.com/TedTschopp/tedt.org/actions/runs/40239758828) and all CodeQL checks pass on `be08fb93d`. Deployment is skipped for the draft PR.
- Production `bundle exec jekyll build` passes; all 986 article pages pass canonical forms, author/content/date metadata, response rendering, and accessible-control checks.
- 28 protocol/moderation/lifecycle/state tests, 4 artifact-handling tests, 11 Webmention/Mastodon browser tests, and 31 existing Mastodon unit tests pass. Mobile controls and slide discussions pass scoped WCAG checks, including both slide themes.
- Editorial credits, publication dates, page SEO, structured-data roles, profile rendering, slide contracts, Mastodon integration, and repository guard pass.
- Pages-format archive parsing reproduces the exact source/target snapshot for all 986 canonical articles, including Unicode and long filenames.
- Read-only endpoint discovery succeeds for all 23 Webmention Rocks cases. No live delivery/conformance claim.
- Compatible HTMLProofer invocation reports 47 existing failures versus 48 on the current main baseline, with no introduced failures; the shared protocol-relative avatar URL is corrected. The existing CI command still uses an unsupported `--check-html` flag.

See [the operations runbook](https://github.com/TedTschopp/tedt.org/blob/be08fb93d4d699e73341018738627ddc3c5596e7/docs/indieweb.md) and the included ADR. After merge/deployment, qualify controlled receive/update/remove and outgoing delivery; reconnect Bridgy interactively if required. Publishing/reader tooling, media hosting, and federation remain later phases.

Inside the article:

• How to build an “agent-first” enterprise
• What metrics matter (CVO, autonomy index, escape rate, MTTR for agents)
• How to architect verification-first systems
• Why human flourishing must remain the destination—not an afterthought

The shift is what I call the Intelligence Inversion:

When turning tokens into work is trivial, the strategic frontier becomes turning work into verified outcomes at scale.

Cheaper brains don’t guarantee better businesses.
